Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later.
See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings#how-claude-code-combines-managed-sources

modelPricing.description:
Report spend at your organization's contracted rates instead of list price, in /usage, the status line, the Agent SDK's total_cost_usd, the --max-budget-usd limit, and OpenTelemetry cost metrics and events. You supply the rates yourself. Managed settings only; ignored in user, project, and local settings, in --settings, and in the Windows HKCU registry. Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later.
See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs#report-spend-at-your-contracted-rates

multiplier.description: Scales every cost Claude Code computes, whether or not an overrides row covers it. Applied on top of a row's own rates when both are set.

overrides.description:
Map of model ID to its USD-per-million-token rates. The ID can be a built-in model ID, its Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry ID, or a gateway model alias.
See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#which-models-a-modelpricing-row-applies-to

cacheWrite.description: USD per million cache-write tokens. Covers both five-minute and one-hour cache writes.

promptCacheTtl.description:
How long the prompt cache holds the main conversation, across interactive, -p, and Agent SDK turns. The one-hour lifetime keeps the cache warm across longer breaks; the API bills each cache write at a higher rate at 1h than at 5m. FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M and the CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL environment variable take precedence over this key, which in turn takes precedence over ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H. Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later.
See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching#cache-lifetime

promptSuggestionEnabled.description:
Show or hide prompt suggestions, the grayed-out predictions in your prompt input. Prompt suggestions need a claude.ai or Console account with telemetry on; on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, or with telemetry off, this key has no effect and only CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_PROMPT_SUGGESTION=1 turns them on.
See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#prompt-suggestions

remote.description:
Settings for cloud sessions you create from the CLI.
See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#remote-defaultenvironmentid

defaultEnvironmentId.description:
Default cloud environment for cloud sessions you create from the CLI, such as with claude --cloud. Claude Code writes this key to your user settings when you pick an environment with /remote-env. An Anthropic-hosted ID (env_...) follows standard settings precedence; a self-hosted environment ID (ccpool_...) is honored only from user settings, managed settings, and --settings, and is ignored in a repository's project or local settings. The --environment flag takes precedence for one session.
See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#remote-defaultenvironmentid

skipAutoPermissionPrompt.description:
Skip the one-time notice describing auto mode that Claude Code shows when you first enter auto mode yourself, rather than when the built-in default starts a session in it. User or managed settings only, so a repository cannot set it for you.
See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#eliminate-prompts-with-auto-mode

spellcheck.description:
Underline misspelled words in the prompt input as you type, using a spell checker you install. Claude Code checks only the text in the input box. When unset, spell checking is off. User or managed settings only; the block from the highest tier that sets it applies as a whole. Requires Claude Code v2.1.235 or later.
See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#check-spelling-as-you-type

checker.description: Which spell checker to use. "auto" picks the first of the three found on PATH.

language.description: Dictionary name passed to the checker. Defaults to the checker's own dictionary.

color.description: Terminal color for the underline: a terminal color name, #rrggbb, rgb(r,g,b), ansi256(n), or ansi:<name>. Defaults to the theme's error color.

subagentPromptCacheTtl.description:
How long the prompt cache holds requests Claude Code makes outside the main conversation: subagents, workflows, and background work such as compaction and session titles. FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M and the CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL environment variable take precedence over this key, which in turn takes precedence over ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H. Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later.
See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching#cache-lifetime

switchModelsOnFlag.description:
What happens when a safety classifier flags a request: true switches to the fallback model and continues; false pauses in an interactive session so you can choose between switching and editing the prompt, or ends the flagged request as an error where no dialog can show. Requires Claude Code v2.1.170 or later.
See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config#ask-before-switching

syncClaudeAiSkills.description:
Turn off the download of the skills you enable on claude.ai, which Claude Code downloads into ~/.claude/skills/synced/ during a non-interactive -p run with CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_SKILLS set. Only false has an effect: it stops the download and hides the skills it already synced. true is the same as unset and does not turn syncing on. User, local, or managed settings only, so a repository cannot turn it off for you.
See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#how-synced-skills-behave

terminalTitleFromRename.description:
Whether naming a session with /rename or --name also changes the terminal tab title to that name. false keeps the title Claude Code generates from your conversation even after you name the session. To stop Claude Code from updating the terminal title at all, set CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE=1 instead.
See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions#name-your-sessions

ultracode.description:
Start sessions with ultracode on, so Claude plans a workflow for each substantive task without being asked, provided dynamic workflows are enabled for you and your model supports xhigh effort. Either way, true runs the session at xhigh effort and takes precedence over effortLevel. Claude Code reads this key but never writes it; /effort ultracode turns ultracode on for the current session only.
See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#let-claude-decide-with-ultracode
